statement_record.book: Every homotopical category C has an associated homotopy category HoC, characterized by the universal property of being initial among categories E equipped with a homotopical functor C -> E (a functor carrying the weak equivalences of C to isomorphisms); the universal functor gamma : C -> HoC is the localization functor. A footnote flags that in the interesting cases C is large and HoC is a priori not locally small.
statement_record.intree: Theorem localization_universal : { G' : Su ⟶ E & (G ≈ G' ◯ Refl) * (∀ H : Su ⟶ E, G ≈ H ◯ Refl → H ≈ G') } — i.e. every W-inverting G : C ⟶ E factors as G' ◯ (reflector R) with G' unique up to natural isomorphism (functor-setoid ≈ in [Su,E] IS natural iso, Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso); complemented by Theorem reflector_inverts_W : IsIsomorphism (fmap[reflector R] w) for every w in W, so the in-tree localization functor is itself W-inverting.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: three genuine hypotheses/weakenings. (1) EXISTENCE IS ASSUMED, NOT PROVED — the in-tree localization exists only when the full subcategory C_W W of W-local objects is REFLECTIVE (`Context (R : Reflective (C_W W))`); Riehl asserts HoC exists for EVERY homotopical category (via the Gabriel-Zisman construction, which the header of Universal.v:34-37 declares out of scope, ledger entry 15). (2) EXTRA HYPOTHESIS `Hunit`: the reflection units must themselves lie in W — the file's own 'honest saturation condition making C_W W the localization AT W'. (3) UNIQUENESS IS UP TO NATURAL ISOMORPHISM (`H ≈ G'` in the functor setoid), whereas Riehl's initiality gives a strict bijection between functors HoC -> E and W-inverting functors C -> E; the in-tree statement gives no bijection and does not identify the factorization on the nose. Not weaker in one respect: W is an arbitrary MorphismClass, so no 2-of-6 hypothesis is needed. The size footnote is a non-issue here — the library is universe-polymorphic and the reflective reading sidesteps the smallness questions (Localization.v:92-94).

gap: The homotopy category is realized only in the REFLECTIVE (orthogonal-subcategory) form: HoC is taken to be the full subcategory C_W W of W-local objects, and its existence is a HYPOTHESIS (`Reflective (C_W W)`) rather than a theorem, so no homotopy category is constructed for a general homotopical category. The universal property additionally requires that the reflection units lie in W (`Hunit`), and delivers uniqueness only up to natural isomorphism rather than the strict initiality (bijection of functor sets) that Definition 6.4.5 states. Nothing in-tree names a 'homotopy category', a 'localization functor gamma' attached to a class of weak equivalences, or proves initiality in the category of categories under C.
